title: The Business of Belonging: How Punjab Kings Converts Attention into Revenue
dek: Fans give Punjab Kings their attention; the franchise has to give them reasons. The measurable part is the cricket itself: winning, drama and big hitting.
excerpt: Punjab Kings have reached the playoffs in a measurable share of their seasons, and their matches have been about as close as the IPL average. Revenue data is not in the warehouse; the on-field product is.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: Attention Is Earned on the Field
body: A franchise turns attention into revenue through tickets, sponsorship, merchandise and media. All of those rest on the same thing: a product people want to watch. For a cricket team, that product is winning, tension and spectacle.
On the first of those, Punjab Kings have reached the playoffs in {{ev:bb-playoffs}} of {{ev:bb-n-seasons}} seasons, with {{ev:bb-titles}} titles.

sections.heading: Drama and Spectacle
body: Close finishes keep audiences to the last ball. {{ev:bb-close}} of Punjab Kings' decided matches were close, against {{ev:bb-lgclose}} across the league.
Big hitting is the other draw: Punjab Kings' matches have averaged {{ev:bb-six}} sixes, both sides combined, against {{ev:bb-lgsix}} across all IPL matches. The chart tracks both by season.

sections.heading: From Attention to Revenue
body: The commercial step from attention to money happens off the field, through pricing, partnerships and content. That step is where franchises differ most, and where the data here stops.

sections.heading: What the Warehouse Cannot See
body: The CricField warehouse is ball-by-ball cricket data. It contains no revenue, attendance, viewership or social-media data, so it cannot measure the commercial side of this question directly.
Testing how on-field results convert into revenue would need franchise financial statements, broadcast audience figures and ticketing data by match.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Protect the Product
body: The part of the business Punjab Kings fully control on the field is the product: competitive seasons, tense matches and entertaining cricket.
Any commercial strategy should start from that product, because every revenue line depends on it.
